title: Run-rate variance & procurement 1:1 prep (mid-Q3) - scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with VP Finance (Marcus) — focus: run-rate variance, upcoming procurement approvals, quick wins for Q3 cost containment.

Key context (quick bullets):
- Feb actual monthly spend (infra + cloud + SaaS): $1.44M. Running 12% MoM increase from Jan driven by hosted API traffic + dedicated burst usage.
- Trailing 3-month average: $1.31M/mo. Latest forecast (baseline) for end of Q3 = $1.58M/mo if no mitigation.
- Major levers: GPU reserved commit (big lever, procurement-heavy), caching/batching config (engineering ops), embedding compute offload windows, SaaS license consolidations.

Top agenda items (30 min):
1) Quick run-rate snapshot (5m) — call out variance vs plan and largest drivers.
2) Procurement approvals pending (10m) — list & ask for priority/expedite guidance.
3) Proposed short-term mitigations (10m) — quick wins we can ask teams to enact.
4) Action items and sign-off timeline (5m).

Run-rate delta breakdown (notes for convo):
- Traffic growth (hosted API): +$60k/mo vs plan — primarily top-10 customers (2 on Dedicated trial).
- Dedicated capacity autoscale spikes (burst): +$38k/mo — irregular but high single-day peaks.
- New model onboarding (bigger memory footprints): +$24k/mo in GPU hours.
- Other (SaaS renewals, tooling): +$20k/mo.

Procurement items awaiting approvals (sorted by risk/amount):
- Aurora GPU cluster (Q3 reserved commit): Quote $360k/yr (approx $30k/mo). Need PO and legal T&Cs signoff.
  - Risk: if deferred, spot/ondemand cost likely +30% for remainder of year.
- CoreCache (edge caching layer) annual contract: $95k/yr. ROI model attached in GDrive sheet.
- Observability retention bump (LogStore): $48k/yr — negotiation in progress, procurement requested 3% discount.
- Multiple SaaS renewals (Datadog/PagerDuty backup licenses): combined $42k/yr — consolidate seats to save ~15%.

Questions to ask Marcus in the 1:1:
- Which procurement items can be fast-tracked by VP signoff vs require exec committee? (PO thresholds: $100k needs VP, >$250k exec?)
- Appetite for temporary hiring freeze in infra for remainder of quarter (saves ~$45k/mo) to hit run-rate targets?
- Comfort level with approving Aurora commit now vs rolling purchases over next 2 quarters?

Short-term mitigations we can implement immediately (engineerable or policy changes):
- Apply conservative batching profile to hosting tier B (expected -8% token cost) — ENG lead: Priya (ETA 7 days).
- Enforce burst-cap cap policy for Dedicated test accounts — Platform Eng to set soft cap (ETA 3 days).
- Pause non-critical model rollouts for two weeks (reduces immediate GPU churn).
- Begin seat consolidation for non-core SaaS (Finance -> run export, deadline 5 business days).

Notes on approvals process (internal steps):
- Create procurement packet (cost, SOW, legal redlines) -> attach to JIRA FIN-342 -> route to Marcus for VP signoff -> if >$250k add exec review (timeline +7 business days).
- For Aurora commit, ask vendor for 14-day hold on pricing while we complete internal review.

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Draft procurement packet for Aurora (content: cost model, fallback plan, vendor SLA) — owner: Ivy — due: 2026-03-15 — status: in progress.
- Run quick ROI for CoreCache (screenshot + model) — owner: Priya Desai — due: 2026-03-13 — status: requested.
- Engineering: implement batching pilot on tier B for 1 week — owner: Priya — due: 2026-03-19 — status: planning.
- Platform Eng: add soft burst cap on Dedicated test accounts — owner: Marcus Lee (platform) — due: 2026-03-17 — status: asked.
- Finance: consolidate SaaS seat lists and propose cuts — owner: Ivy — due: 2026-03-18 — status: backlog.

Follow-ups to track after the 1:1:
- If VP signs Aurora PO, route to Legal and Procurement and cc vendor within 48h.
- If Aurora delayed, prepare spot-cost contingency and estimate delta for remainder of year (owner: finance ops).
- Send one-pager to execs if >$250k requires committee (Ivy to draft).

Loose notes / talking points (short phrases to use in meeting):
- "We have a path to a 6–8% run-rate reduction within 30 days using non-headcount levers."
- "Aurora commit reduces unit GPU cost by approx 18% vs spot — tradeoff is capital timing."
- "Short-term policy controls easier to implement than hiring changes; want to reserve hiring ask as last resort."

Quick links (for screen share):
- GDrive run-rate model: shared_drives/finance-and-legal/q3-burn-model.xlsx
- JIRA FIN-342 (procurement packet)
- Slack thread: #finance-runrate (pin: latest Feb spend run)

Meeting finish checklist (after 1:1):
- Confirm which POs to escalate and by when.
- Publish action-item tracker in Slack channel and tag owners.
- Update run-rate model with any approvals/deferrals.

Scratchpad notes end — leave this doc as the temporary single-source prep for the call.
mini_summary: Prep for 1:1 with VP Finance to review mid-Q3 run-rate variance, list procurement approvals (Aurora, CoreCache, LogStore), propose short-term mitigations (batching, caps, seat consolidation), and assign action items for sign-off timeline.
